I find it ridiculous that there are positive comments.
In my opinion, this is a regrettable mistake and a money pit.
I placed my trust in this clinic for gallbladder removal surgery for my dog.
After the surgery, I visited the dog in recovery and he seemed to be able to overcome the post-operative period. (I even have a video)
During the morning I received a call informing me that the dog had died because he couldn't regulate his sugar levels, without further explanation.
So if he was in Intensive Care/Recovery, shouldn't he have been monitored and corrected in all parameters?
Explanations practically zero. Someone showed up, but only to have me fill out paperwork.
The only thing that resulted from this was a bill of almost four thousand euros, including cremation, for two days of stay, and my faithful companion lifeless in my arms, with his eyes open, as if he were looking for me.
A trauma that will stay with me.
Run away from these individuals.
One star is too much for the service they provide.

Doctor Hugo Lucas in neurology has taken exceptional care of Mel who had a stroke. Within the clinic all nurses and doctors communicate with each other aiding in her recovery. Mel’s recovery plan made by Dr. Hugo Lucas was great and throughly explained which made us feel very reassured. At every appointment we felt like we understood what was going on with Mel and understood what we can expect from her recovery and treatments. Dr. Hugo Lucas was always available to answer any of our questions in person and through email which greatly alleviated our stress through these hard times. Overall we are very thankful to the wonderful nurses and doctors in this clinic that showed genuine care for Mel at her physiotherapy, appointments and during her hospitalization. Everyone showed amazing professionalism, knowledge, care and empathy. We always felt that Mel was in the best of hands and the team was doing everything possible to aid in her recovery.
Exceptional

Positive Aspects:

Excellent professionals, very well organized, caring, direct, friendly and, above all, very dedicated.

They demonstrate that they really know what they are doing. They helped my four-legged companion whenever necessary, with professionalism and dedication. I can only thank them and say: thank you very much, AniCura!

Less Positive Aspects:

The emergency fee of €112, applied during the night (from 8/9 pm until 9 am the following day), as well as on Sundays and holidays all day, is quite high.

It's not a cheap hospital, but, in my opinion, quality comes at a price — and quality is something AniCura has.

Another less positive point is the difficulty in getting through by phone. However, after some reflection, it becomes clear that this situation makes sense: it's a hospital prepared to receive emergencies 24 hours a day, and if they were constantly answering calls, they probably wouldn't be able to give the proper attention to the animals they are treating.

Despite this, they always respond to emails and, in cases of hospitalization, they make a point of calling daily to provide updates on the animals' progress. This is something I consider very positive.

Finally, the reception areas for clients are a bit small, especially considering the volume of patients and the fact that it's a 24-hour emergency hospital.

Overall, my experience is very positive. I recommend AniCura and thank all the professionals for their work, dedication, and care.
Excessive waiting time/delay.

This was confirmed, and after a 3-hour wait, he was examined and the matter was more or less treated. Today I had to go to another veterinarian because Thor wouldn't stop scratching and biting himself and has dermatitis. I left my cat there early on a Saturday morning. The treatment they said they would provide was completely inadequate; on the contrary, they gave vitamins to stimulate the appetite of a cat with compromised liver function, and they knew this. Anyone who understands the subject knows that these vitamins are not suitable for animals with compromised liver function. I had no input in this decision. They kept the cat in their facilities for well over 12 hours without food and couldn't provide a valid justification for the situation. They never contacted me to find out what I wanted to do. The only indication I gave was that I wanted the esophageal feeding tube to be inserted by her veterinarian. From then on, seeing that they weren't going to bill what they initially thought they would, the quality of care declined. They were even surprised when I, her owner, without knowing anything and without having done what they said they would do during hospitalization (and they didn't feed her), raised my voice when my pet was discharged to the veterinarian Diana Fernandes, who spent the entire consultation, both on the phone and in person, breathing heavily. Every time I asked them a question or made a complaint, they acted with tremendous arrogance, especially since they call between 11 am and 3 pm to give feedback on hospitalized animals, and it wasn't until 2:50 pm that they called me to say she hadn't eaten since the previous day. I don't live near Restelo, so the time between the contact and discharge was the time it took me to get dressed and travel time. If they had contacted me earlier, I would have taken the cat out of there immediately to take her to her veterinarian. As for emergencies, I don't recommend anyone with cats go there. If you have cats, it's better to go to the cat hospital; they'll be better served there. As far as I'm concerned, my animal will only stay there in the emergency system if there's no other alternative. Even the discharge report wasn't done properly, and I had to ask them to redo it. We entrust our animals to these people, and then they do what they want and not what they discussed with the animal's owner. And they wanted to charge over €800 for a hospitalization that had been agreed upfront wouldn't last more than two days because they would pick her up afterwards to take her back to her vet, and then they would have to refund over €600. Luckily, I paid less and they only have to refund €40 and some cents, which on Tuesday was supposed to take 4 days. So far I haven't received anything; the 4 days are just for show. I've never seen my dog ​​so agitated as when she was discharged from this place. As soon as she arrived at her vet, they fed her and she calmed down – what a surprise! It's a huge contrast for someone who had a consultation with Dr. Martinho Capelão in orthopedics and then encounters this. I wasn't expecting such poor service at all. Now I can guarantee that, as far as I'm concerned, I won't go back there except in specific situations and with certain doctors.
Been calling the hospital for months, staying on line for hours, no one ever picks up, calls back or respond. The doctors are recommended, but the administration is non existent.

I don't know if there are enough words of gratitude to describe how happy we felt after our consultation with Dr. Doroteia Bota. It wasn't just a consultation with a top-level professional. We entrusted our dog, her problems, complaints, and our anxiety to the careful hands of true specialists. Knowing we came from another city, Dr. Doroteia Bota performed absolutely all the tests and analyses, took the opportunity, and immediately referred us to specific specialists for further examinations. Our beloved dog was examined almost from nose to tail. And all this took no more than 3 hours. All the examinations were thoroughly justified and explained meticulously. Considering our previous attempts at other clinics, with other doctors and in other cities, everything done here was a happy demonstration of professionalism, love for our dog, empathy, and the desire to save us wasted time. Less than 10 hours had passed since the visit, and we already knew the results of the analyses and exams, the underlying cause of the worsening health, the treatment plan, what to feed our dog, and the treatment control dates. Dr. Doroteia Bota called us and explained literally everything: the values ​​of the analysis results, the reports, the entire mechanism of the disease, and the current state of our dog. We are especially grateful for this call, as we were very anxious while waiting. And yes, we consider that fate gave our beloved Mania a gift when she crossed paths with such a humane, professional doctor, possessing advanced knowledge, with a sincere heart, understanding, and compassion as Dr. Doroteia Bota. From now on, we are at peace regarding the life and health of our dog. Thank you for your work!
With great respect for the professionalism of Dr. Doroteia Bota and immense gratitude for the work of the entire clinic team. Stoliarov-Somodi Family.

An absolutely disappointing and, in my opinion, unacceptable experience for an emergency veterinary service. We arrived with our puppy in our arms, practically collapsed and barely able to stand. We waited quite a while at reception without anyone even approaching us to ask what was wrong or to assess his condition. Finally, after explaining the situation, we were told that there were three animals ahead of us and that the wait would be between two and three hours. I completely understand that emergencies are treated according to severity and that there can be very critical cases, but what I cannot understand is that no one, neither a veterinarian nor the staff, came out to make a quick assessment or give us any guidance on what to do during that waiting time, seeing the state our dog was in. The feeling was one of a complete lack of empathy and consideration. Given the impression that if we waited those two or three hours, our puppy might not make it, we were forced to leave to seek help elsewhere. I hope you review your reception and triage protocols, because when someone comes with an animal in such a delicate state, the least they expect is for a professional to assess and guide them as soon as possible.

Their professionalism, competence, empathy, and care throughout the entire process were truly unsurpassed. We always felt informed, heard, and supported, even during our most worrying moments.

I also want to highlight the reception staff, who are extraordinarily kind and helpful. They always greet us with a smile, are tireless in their assistance, and make us feel welcome.

One of the aspects I value most is the ease of contact with the clinical team. Whenever a question arises, whether by email or phone, the response is quick, clear, and reassuring.

Although we are still undergoing treatment, we have never doubted that we made the right choice. I recommend AniCura Restelo without hesitation to anyone looking for an excellent team, not only for their high technical level, but above all for the humanity, dedication and care with which they treat the animals and their families.

I'm letting everyone know that if you intend to take your animal to this renowned and well-known Veterinary Hospital, whether referred or not, and request appointments for urgent procedures or not, it won't make any difference to them.

After several days in which our dog Hope Maria was having ataxic seizures, neck stiffness, and becoming very weak, we had the support of the staff at the AniCura Hospital in Arco do Cego, who were spectacular and 5 stars.

After many attempts with other clinics to schedule an MRI for our Hope, and with the help of the AniCura team in Arco do Cego, they managed to schedule it for the next day (May 7th at 12 pm) due to the urgency of a concrete diagnosis for the dog, who was suffering.

Well, we took the dog to AniCura Restelo as the AniCura Arco do Cego team had informed us; we had the chart with the vital signs, clinical details, and the therapy the dog was following.

Upon being attended to, the receptionist informed us that we should have scheduled an appointment with a neurologist before we could have the MRI done. We explained that we had been referred from Arco do Cego and that we had been informed that they would have the information about the dog, the appointment, and the urgency of her condition. The receptionist said that there was nothing for that day related to our dog. Apparently, there was no internal communication, no information was passed on, which is regrettable and unjustifiable.
In the midst of this urgent situation with the dog in my arms, the receptionist still asked me to fill out a form about the anesthesia, and she insisted that I fill out and sign the form and the invoice. I even had to make the payment... all this with the dog completely stiff in my lap. This service was quite insensitive.
Then the receptionist informed us that the dog would be put on the waiting list to have the procedure done. After mentioning that it was an emergency and because she had been referred, we asked if it would be possible for her procedure to be expedited and done as soon as possible. The girl went inside the hospital to confirm with Dr. Hugo Lucas and confirmed again that she would be the first. I asked to leave the dog in the preparation area for the MRI, but the receptionist wouldn't let us take the dog, which was in distress, and insisted that we needed to take it. There was no tact in attending to us; they were always trying to rush us and admit people's animals, to such an extent that the animals seemed like just another procedure on the line. It was sad.

I highly doubt she was the first, because after we informed the staff at Arco do Cego by phone about the whole situation, which was around 3:33 pm, I received a call 20 minutes later from Dr. Luís Carvalho from AniCura Restelo (I had mentioned Dr. Hugo Lucas earlier, but I don't know what happened; they were so uninformed that they couldn't even tell us about the doctor), just saying that the procedure was over and that it was a very complicated situation because he had found a mass in Hope's brain and that he didn't have much more to say, without any tact, empathy, or sensitivity. We tried to ask to speak for a few minutes at reception, and he told us he couldn't because he was busy and had other procedures to do. That call didn't last 3 minutes, so you can get an idea of ​​how rushed things are. It's not about the money, but we receive this kind of service and treatment when we pay almost €800 for the procedure and the urgency.

It took just over 3 hours from admission to the phone call, and they told me to pick up the dog at 5:30 PM. Honestly, I don't understand what happened during all that time, and I don't understand what's going on with these people. Given all this, here is my criticism of the AniCura Restelo Veterinary Hospital: lack of professionalism and humanity in their service. If you are looking for humane and empathetic care during your pet's difficult times, and if you, as pet owners, value competence and professionalism, I do not recommend them.

Besides being super professional, she was also a sweetheart, and if my cat's problem had been resolved there, I wouldn't be giving such a low rating.

A week or so after this first consultation, my cat started having the same symptoms again, and I called the hospital to explain the situation and ask if I should start administering the antibiotics. They told me no, and that I should take her back there to have a urine sample taken. I went there again and my cat was seen by Dr. André Santos, who collected a urine sample and gave a timeframe of a few days until the test results were ready, and that he would contact me afterwards. In addition, he prescribed more anti-inflammatory medication and told me to give it to my cat for 6 days this time.
After 3 days, my cat started vomiting the medication, and I called the hospital again. Since Dr. André wasn't there, I had to speak to another doctor, who thought it was absurd to give anti-inflammatory medication for so many days and told me to stop that day, also prescribing medication for nausea and vomiting.
The day they were supposed to call with the test results arrived, and nothing. The next day I called the hospital, and they told me that the doctor had already called the previous day and talked about the tests, which left me extremely confused. Upon insisting, the receptionist realized that not only had the doctor called my boyfriend, who didn't answer, but the doctor hadn't tried to call me, even though my cat's file was in my name, and I had to wait longer this time because the doctor wasn't at the hospital yet. When he finally called me, hours later, he said that my cat did indeed have a little blood in her urine as well as crystals, but that both were normal and that she would recover with just the anti-inflammatory. I then asked if, in case she got worse again, I could start giving her the antibiotic that Dr. Sofia had prescribed, to which he said that, in that case, my cat would have to have another urine sample taken because the result could be a "false negative".

In summary and conclusion, my cat has had the same symptoms again for a few days, and I came from the Ajuda Veterinary Clinic today, where they were shocked that my cat hadn't taken antibiotics, that the Restelo hospital hadn't sent me the results of the urine tests, and that they hadn't even talked about the type of diet she should have (in this case, for urinary tract issues).
It's not very useful to have nice facilities and an Instagram page if they then rush through certain cases.
Fortunately, my cat is now being monitored in the right place and with the proper care, but I hope there aren't more urgent/delicate situations with other people's pets, where they might suffer the consequences of "professionals" who treat the health of our best friends as a business.

I recently took my 8-year-old dog to this veterinary hospital after he suddenly lost his sight. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and I appreciate them treating us on an emergency basis. I was informed that the emergency consultation would cost €52, but after they performed some tests and suggested a blood test, the total bill came to €269. As I don't have pet health insurance, I asked at reception if a discount would be possible. They spoke to the doctor and kindly reduced the price to around €178, which I appreciate.

However, what happened next was disappointing. I waited three days for the lab results, but when I contacted them by email, they informed me that they hadn't sent the blood for analysis after all, due to the costs. This decision was never communicated to me at the time. Furthermore, they didn't schedule any follow-up or treatment plan, leaving me without guidance on what to do next.

Although the service was friendly and the initial care prompt, I consider it unethical that they did not inform me that they decided not to proceed with the tests after payment, especially when those results would be fundamental in guiding the treatment. Transparency and follow-up are essential, particularly when it comes to the health of a pet and the concerns of its owners.
